the statistical significance of a shift in atmospheric temperatures, and the physical mechanisms behind the shift.

the observed shift in the European climate around 1987/1988 is not a statistically significant change in the European temperature regime, but is a fingerprint of European climate brightening during the past few decades.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found no evidence for any statistically robust change in climate in Europe around 1988, but rather a change in the climate statistics, i.e. a change in the distribution of the climate variables.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a shift in temperature is not necessarily a fingerprint of a climate shift, but could also be caused by a change in external climate forcings.
a shift in temperature is not a good indicator of a change in the climate state.
it is important to consider the effect of brightening/dimming on the interpretation of climate change signals, especially in Europe, where this effect has been substantial.
